question.prompt: Suppose \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are points in the plane with \(AB = 40\) and \(AC = 42,\) and let \(x\) be the length of the line segment from \(A\) to the midpoint of \(\overline{BC}.\) Define a function \(f\) by letting \(f(x)\) be the area of \(\triangle ABC.\) Then the domain of \(f\) is an open interval \((p, q),\) and the maximum value \(r\) of \(f(x)\) occurs at \(x = s.\) What is \(p + q + r + s?\)

solutions.title: Double the median
solutions.explanation:
Doubling the median creates a triangle whose other two sides have lengths \(40\) and \(42\), allowing us to bound \(x\) directly.

Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(BC\). Extend \(AM\) through \(M\) to a point \(D\) with \(MD=AM=x\). The diagonals \(AD\) and \(BC\) bisect each other, so \(ABDC\) is a parallelogram. In particular, \(CD=AB=40\). Thus triangle \(ACD\) has side lengths \(42,40,2x\).

The strict triangle inequalities give
\[
42-40<2x<42+40,
\]
so \(1<x<41\). Conversely, any triangle with sides \(42,40,2x\) can be completed to this parallelogram by reflecting \(C\) across the midpoint of \(AD\). Therefore every \(x\) in this interval is possible. The endpoints give collinear points and are excluded. Hence
\[
p=1,\qquad q=41.
\]

To maximize the area of \(ABC\), use \(AB=40\) as the base. The perpendicular height from \(C\) to line \(AB\) is at most \(AC=42\), with equality exactly when \(AC\perp AB\). Consequently,
\[
r=\frac12(40)(42)=840.
\]
At this maximum, triangle \(ABC\) is right at \(A\), so
\[
BC=\sqrt{40^2+42^2}=58.
\]
The median to the hypotenuse of a right triangle has half the hypotenuse's length. Thus \(s=58/2=29\).

Therefore
\[
p+q+r+s=1+41+840+29=\boxed{911},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

solutions.title: Write the area in terms of the median
solutions.explanation:
The median formula expresses \(BC\) in terms of \(x\). Heron's formula can then reveal the maximum area by completing a square.

Write \(a=BC\). Adding the cosine-law equations for triangles \(ABM\) and \(ACM\), where \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), cancels the cosine terms because the angles at \(M\) are supplementary. This gives the median identity
\[
40^2+42^2=2x^2+\frac{a^2}{2},
\]
and hence
\[
a^2=6728-4x^2.
\]
The side lengths \(40,42,a\) form a nondegenerate triangle exactly when \(2<a<82\). Substitution gives
\[
4<6728-4x^2<6724,
\]
or \(1<x<41\). Every such value produces a valid third side, so \(p=1\) and \(q=41\).

Let \(K\) denote the area and let \(u=(82+a)/2\) be the semiperimeter. Heron's formula, \(K^2=u(u-40)(u-42)(u-a)\), gives
\[
16K^2=(82^2-a^2)(a^2-2^2).
\]
Replacing \(a^2\) by \(6728-4x^2\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
K^2&=(x^2-1)(1681-x^2)\\
&=840^2-(x^2-841)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The subtracted square is nonnegative, so \(K\le840\). Equality occurs when \(x^2=841\), giving \(x=29\), which lies in the domain. Thus \(r=840\) and \(s=29\).

Therefore
\[
p+q+r+s=1+41+840+29=\boxed{911},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
